matchstick.title: Preserve stick orientation
matchstick.principle: When moving a matchstick, keep its orientation (vertical, horizontal, or diagonal) unchanged; you cannot rotate a stick.
matchstick.example: Rotating a diagonal stick to become vertical, resulting in an invalid character.

matchstick.title: No addition or removal of sticks
matchstick.principle: Exactly one existing stick must be moved; you cannot create a new stick or discard a stick without placing it elsewhere.
matchstick.example: Removing a stick from a numeral and not placing it anywhere, effectively deleting it.

matchstick.title: Maintain valid characters
matchstick.principle: After the move, every symbol must still be a legal Roman numeral (I, V, X, L, C, D, M) or an allowed operator (+, -, =).
matchstick.when_to_apply: After any relocation, check each character.
matchstick.example: Leaving a single diagonal after taking one from a V, which is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.title: Verify arithmetic correctness
matchstick.principle: Compute the Arabic values of both sides of the transformed equation and confirm they are equal.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After proposing a transformation, before final answer.
matchstick.example: Accepting 'XV = XV - XV' without noticing it evaluates to 15 = 0.

matchstick.title: Operator swap via stick exchange
matchstick.principle: You may move a stick from one operator to another, changing both operators, provided the resulting symbols are valid operators.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the only viable source of a stick is an operator and the destination is another operator.
matchstick.example: Moving a horizontal from '=' to '+' and ending up with an invalid operator shape.

matchstick.title: Do not break X or V
matchstick.principle: Never leave an X or V with only one diagonal after moving a stick; the remaining single diagonal does not form a valid numeral.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When considering removing a diagonal from X or V.
matchstick.example: Removing one diagonal from X, leaving a single diagonal.

matchstick.title: Cross‑numeral stick transfer
matchstick.principle: A stick can be moved from one numeral to another, but both the source and destination must remain valid Roman numerals after the move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a stick can be taken from one numeral and added to a different numeral.
matchstick.example: Taking a vertical from I and adding it to V, resulting in an invalid shape.

matchstick.title: Within‑numeral stick repositioning
matchstick.principle: A stick may be moved to a different location within the same numeral, changing its shape (e.g., V ↔ X) while preserving orientation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a single stick can be repositioned inside a numeral to form another valid numeral.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal within V but leaving it as a single diagonal, which is invalid.

matchstick.title: Equality sign preservation
matchstick.principle: The equation must contain exactly one '=' sign after the move; you cannot turn it into another operator or alter its shape.
matchstick.example: Removing a horizontal from '=', turning it into '-' and losing the equality.

matchstick.title: Operator-to-numeral stick transfer
matchstick.principle: When moving a stick from an operator to a numeral, the operator must remain a valid operator after losing the stick (e.g., '+' can become '-', but cannot become an invalid shape), and the numeral must become a valid Roman numeral after gaining the stick.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the only source of a stick is an operator and the destination is a numeral.
matchstick.example: Moving the vertical stick from '+' to a numeral but ending up with an invalid numeral or leaving '+' as an unsupported shape.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on making the symbols look correct but forgets to compute the numeric values, leading to equations that are syntactically valid but arithmetically false.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always compute the Arabic values of both sides after any transformation and ensure they are equal before finalizing the answer.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model moves a stick in a way that adds or removes an operator, resulting in too many or too few operators in the equation.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Keep the number of operators unchanged; moving a stick should not create or delete an operator symbol.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model moves a stick away from an operator without ensuring the remaining sticks still form a valid operator shape, resulting in an invalid operator such as a lone vertical line or a missing operator.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Before moving a stick from an operator, verify that the operator's required stick composition still matches a valid operator after the removal (e.g., '+' can lose its vertical to become '-', but cannot lose its horizontal).
